owner_posts.post_text:
What If I don't like the diet plan given to reduce diabetes?

Issues that can make you dislike or feel discontented with diet plan are:
 ✔ If the food ingredients are absolutely new to you or haven't been tried before
 ✔ If the recipes are not practical
 ✔ If the food combinations do not agree with your body
 ✔ If the diet is too restrictive or has very little options
Skipping meals or extreme dieting can worsen blood sugar control.
A scientifically designed diet to reduce diabetes focuses on balance - not restriction.

📞 Book your personalized diabetes consultation.

Does summer affect serum creatinine?

Yes, it does! During summers especially peak temperatures and high physician activities, your body can get dehydrated which can lead to temporary rise in serum creatinine 

Hence, hydration is extremely important
In case you have complains of swelling or elevated BP, then you should discuss with your doctor about daily fluid intake

Next you should discuss with your renal dietitian about fluids distribution throughout the day
To book a kidney diet consultation, call us now

Does Dr Rachana Jasani offer herbal supplements?

At NutriKonnect, we do not offer herbal supplements

The aim is to meet nutrition goals with strategic diet planning

Sometimes, individuals with poor oral intake may need to be supplemented to provide adequate nutrients but those include scientific evidence based formulas


Take charge of your health today, please call us

Struggling with pre-diabetes despite eating fewer calories?

Despite eating lesser calories, many individuals with pre-diabetes struggle to reverse it
The missing link is often protein deficit !
So you need a diabetes diet expert, who can switch from generic advice like eating fewer calories to personalised advice like eating the correct amount of proteins

At NutriKonnect, we offer the below services for diabetes reversal:
✔ Customized meal planning
✔ Practical food choices
✔ Sustainable lifestyle changes

📞 Dont just eat less, eat correct!
Book your appointment today

Is creatinine reversible?

Simple answer:
In case of Acute Kidney Injury: YES, creatinine can be reversed to its normal range

In case of Chronic Kidney Disease: NO, creatinine cannot be reversed to its normal range

But it can be controlled through diet and lifestyle modifications which can act as a supportive line to the medical treatment

In case you need structured guidance to control creatinine from a Certitified Renal Nutritionist, call us now 📞

Do kidney donors need a special diet?

Kidney donors usually ask me this question and it is certainly a relevant one
As a Renal Dietitian, my answer is yes!
They should seek guidance not only for diet also for lifestyle modifications for long term

Who should seek guidance?:
✔Kidney donors who are overweight or obese 
✔Kidney donors who may underlying lipid abnormalities like borderline cholesterol or low levels of good cholesterol (HDL) or high levels of bad cholesterol (LDL/VLDL) 
✔Kidney donors with fatty liver 
✔ Or kidney donors who develop any of the above even years after kidney transplant should seek nutrition guidance

So, if you are a kidney donor; then you have your answer right here !

In case you need personal consultation, call us 📞

Can diabetics eat mangoes?

Certainly yes, mangoes can be incorporated into a diabetic diet plan, but with a few cautionary  tips:
✔Avoid pulp (aam ras)
✔Avoid mangoes with large meals
✔Prefer them during mid -meal time (11 am or 5 pm)
✔Maintain portion control (stick to 3-4 slices)

Smart nutrition strategies is the key to incorporate your favourite foods into your diabetes diet plan without the stress of blood sugar spikes.

With such sustainable options, individuals with pre-diabetes may also be able to easily navigate through their diabetes reversal journey

📞Don't wait, book your appointment today

General Dietitian vs Renal Dietitian - What’s the Difference?

Many people think all dietitians are the same, but they are not

A General Dietitian focuses on:
 - ✔ Weight loss
 - ✔ PCOS
 - ✔ Gut improvement
 - ✔ General well-being

A Renal Dietitian specializes in:
 - ✔ Different stages of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
 - ✔ CKD with diabetes
 - ✔ CKD with obesity, diabetes, and high blood pressure
 - ✔ CKD & diabetes complications
- ✔ Auto-immune conditions involving the kidneys
- ✔ Kidney stones, high uric acid, etc.

Kidney patients need stage-specific medical nutrition therapy.

If you are looking for one of the best renal dietitians to manage your renal health, choose someone with specialized kidney nutrition expertise

Understanding Irregular Periods in PCOS

Irregular periods are one of the most common symptoms of PCOS. Many women experience delayed cycles, missed periods, or unpredictable menstrual patterns, often wondering whether this is normal.

In PCOS, hormonal imbalances can interfere with regular ovulation. When ovulation becomes irregular or does not occur consistently, menstrual cycles may become unpredictable. Elevated insulin levels, inflammation, stress, and lifestyle factors can further contribute to these changes.

While irregular periods are common in PCOS, they should not be ignored. Consistent menstrual irregularities may indicate that the body's hormonal systems are not functioning optimally and may require professional evaluation.

Lifestyle modifications such as maintaining a balanced diet, engaging in regular physical activity, managing stress, and prioritizing sleep can help support hormonal health. Medical and nutritional interventions may also be recommended depending on individual needs.

Early attention to menstrual irregularities can support long-term reproductive and metabolic health. Understanding the underlying causes is the first step toward effective management.

If you experience persistent irregular periods, consult a qualified healthcare professional for a comprehensive assessment and personalized guidance.

PCOS Myth vs Fact: Separating Truth from Misconceptions

There are many misconceptions surrounding PCOS, and misinformation can often create confusion and unnecessary anxiety. Understanding the facts is essential for effective management.

Myth: Women with PCOS cannot become pregnant.

Fact: While PCOS can affect ovulation and fertility, many women with PCOS successfully conceive naturally or with appropriate medical support.

Myth: Only overweight women develop PCOS.

Fact: PCOS can affect women of all body types. Lean PCOS is a recognized condition, and symptoms can occur regardless of body weight.

Myth: Irregular periods are harmless.

Fact: Irregular menstrual cycles may indicate underlying hormonal imbalances and should be properly evaluated by a healthcare professional.

Myth: PCOS only affects reproductive health.

Fact: PCOS can also impact metabolism, cardiovascular health, mental well-being, and long-term quality of life.

The more we understand PCOS, the better equipped we are to manage it effectively. Education, early intervention, healthy lifestyle choices, and professional guidance remain key components of successful management.

Don't let myths shape your understanding of PCOS. Reliable information can empower women to take informed steps toward better health and wellness.

PCOS and Nutrition: Why What You Eat Matters

Nutrition is one of the most powerful tools available for managing PCOS symptoms. Although there is no single diet that works for everyone, food choices can significantly impact hormones, insulin sensitivity, inflammation, and overall health.

Many women with PCOS experience insulin resistance, a condition where the body's cells become less responsive to insulin. This can lead to elevated insulin levels, which may contribute to hormonal imbalances and worsen symptoms such as irregular periods, acne, and weight gain.

A nutrition plan focused on whole foods can make a meaningful difference. High-fiber vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats help support stable blood sugar levels and promote satiety. Reducing excessive intake of sugary beverages, refined carbohydrates, and highly processed foods may also be beneficial.

Hydration, meal timing, physical activity, and adequate sleep are additional factors that support metabolic and hormonal health. Small, consistent lifestyle changes often produce better long-term results than extreme diets.

PCOS management requires a comprehensive approach. Nutrition alone may not eliminate symptoms, but it can play a major role in improving overall well-being and supporting hormonal balance.

If you're looking to take control of your PCOS journey, start by building sustainable habits that support your body's long-term health.

Nutrient of the Week: Myo-Inositol

When discussing nutritional support for PCOS, Myo-Inositol is one of the most researched and widely recommended nutrients. Often referred to as a vitamin-like compound, Myo-Inositol plays a key role in cellular communication, insulin signaling, and ovarian function.

Many women with PCOS experience insulin resistance, which can contribute to hormonal imbalances, irregular menstrual cycles, difficulty with ovulation, and weight management challenges. Myo-Inositol helps support healthy insulin sensitivity, which may positively influence these symptoms.

Research suggests that Myo-Inositol may help improve menstrual regularity, support ovulation, and contribute to better reproductive health in women with PCOS. It may also help support metabolic health when combined with a balanced lifestyle.

While nutrition supplements can provide support, they work best alongside healthy eating habits, regular exercise, adequate sleep, and stress management. Every individual is different, and nutritional needs can vary significantly.

Before starting any supplement, it is important to seek professional guidance to determine what is most appropriate for your specific health goals and condition.

Understanding the science behind nutrients like Myo-Inositol can help women make informed decisions about managing PCOS and improving overall wellness.

Best Nutrients for PCOS Management

PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) affects millions of women worldwide and is often associated with irregular periods, weight gain, acne, excessive hair growth, and fertility challenges. While medical management is important, nutrition plays a crucial role in supporting hormonal balance and improving symptoms.

Certain nutrients have shown promising benefits for women with PCOS. Myo-Inositol is widely recognized for supporting insulin sensitivity and helping regulate menstrual cycles. Vitamin D deficiency is common among women with PCOS, and maintaining adequate levels may support hormonal and metabolic health. Omega-3 fatty acids help reduce inflammation and may support healthy hormone function. Magnesium contributes to blood sugar regulation, stress management, and better sleep quality. Zinc is another valuable nutrient that may help support skin health, hair growth, and reproductive function.

A balanced diet rich in vegetables, fruits, lean proteins, healthy fats, and whole grains can provide many of these nutrients naturally. In some cases, supplementation may be considered under professional guidance.

Managing PCOS is not about following restrictive diets or quick fixes. Consistent nutrition, regular physical activity, stress management, and professional healthcare support can help improve long-term outcomes.

If you're struggling with PCOS symptoms, consult a healthcare professional to develop a personalized nutrition and wellness.

featured_reviews.name: Harsh Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Game-Changer for Health

My Experience with Dietitian Saloni
In July 2025, I received a life-altering diagnosis of AVN (Avascular necrosis of hip).  My doctor stressed the importance of weight loss, as I was 83 kgs at the time.  Simultaneously, blood tests revealed pre-diabetes and high cholesterol – a perfect storm of health concerns.  Feeling overwhelmed, I turned to my baby sister, Dietitian Saloni, for help.
From the very beginning, Saloni's approach was personalized and supportive. She crafted a plan tailored to my eating preferences and daily schedule, making it easy to integrate into my life.  Crucially, she didn't just hand me a diet; she educated me.  She explained the fundamental principles of healthy eating, knowledge that I know will stay with me for life.
As if the initial diagnoses weren't enough, the stress of my AVN diagnosis took a toll on my gut health.  I was incredibly worried, but Saloni was there again, providing expert guidance and support through dietary adjustments and appropriate supplements.
It's now been six months since I started Saloni's plan, and the results speak for themselves. I've lost 7 kgs, and the best part is, I haven't felt starved or deprived.  Saloni's approach is about nourishing my body, not punishing it.  She's helped me understand that healthy eating isn't about restriction, but about balance and making informed choices.  If you're looking for a dietitian who genuinely cares and empowers you to take control of your health, I wholeheartedly recommend Saloni.  She's not just my sister; she's my health champion.

Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a common hormonal disorder that affects people with ovaries, often during their reproductive years. Managing PCOS involves a combination of lifestyle changes, medical treatment, and regular monitoring. Here are some key considerations:

Healthy Diet: Adopting a balanced and nutritious diet can help manage weight and improve insulin sensitivity. Focus on whole foods, including fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains. Limit the intake of processed foods, sugary snacks, and refined carbohydrates.
Regular Exercise: Engage in regular physical activity to help control weight and improve insulin resistance. Both aerobic exercise and strength training can be beneficial. Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise per week.
Weight Management: Achieving and maintaining a healthy weight can positively impact hormonal balance and alleviate symptoms of PCOS. Even a modest weight loss can lead to improvements in menstrual regularity and fertility.

featured_reviews.name: Mikita rupreja
featured_reviews.review_text:
I consulted Neev Nutrition by Ushma Chheda to maintain my weight, and my experience has been really wonderful. Ushma gives healthy yet tasty diet plans with very simple and practical changes that actually work. I could see positive results without feeling like I was following a strict diet.

featured_reviews.name: Sheetal Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
I, Sheetal Shah, would like to share my wonderful experience with Dietitian Ushma Chedda at Neev Nutrition. When I first started my journey, I was struggling with cholesterol and weight issues. Under her expert guidance and well-planned diet, I successfully lost 10 kgs within just three months, and today I feel extremely light, active, and healthy. My cholesterol levels have completely normalized, which has been a life-changing improvement for me.

Not only do I feel healthier from within, but even my face looks brighter and more refreshed. Ushma Chedda is extremely knowledgeable and supportive. She carefully understands your lifestyle, preferences, and health conditions before designing a diet plan, making it very easy and comfortable to follow.

The staff at New Nutrition is also very polite, helpful, and professional. The hospitality is excellent, and everything is managed in a very systematic and organized manner. One of the best parts of the program is the amazing variety of food and snacks provided every week the quality is truly top-notch. Because of this wide variety, the diet never feels boring or restrictive, and it becomes easy to stay consistent.

Ushma Chedda constantly motivates, monitors progress, and makes adjustments whenever required. She creates diet plans that are practical, convenient, and sustainable for long-term health. Her dedication, positive attitude, and personalized care make her an outstanding dietitian. I am truly grateful for her guidance and highly recommend Neev Nutrition to anyone who wants to improve their health in a natural and effective way.

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
I started my journey with Neev when I weighed 103 kg, and today I’m feeling much lighter after losing 11 kg, bringing me down to 92 kg—and I’m motivated to lose even more! 💪✨

A big thank you to Ushma and her wonderful team for supporting me throughout this journey 🙏. When I first visited, my HbA1c levels were borderline high at 6.3, and now they’ve improved to 5.8 🎉. I also have hypothyroidism and am on medication, and Ushma carefully tailored my diet plan to suit my medical condition as well as my food preferences 🥗🧘‍♂️. She also guided me on portion control, which has played a huge role in my weight-loss success.

There were times when, due to medical emergencies, I couldn’t follow the diet. However, the team always suggested practical alternatives for eating outside, which made the journey much easier and stress-free 🍽️👍.

Once again, a heartfelt thank you to Ushma and her team ❤️. I would highly recommend Neev to anyone who is serious about weight loss but doesn’t want to be on an overly strict or unrealistic diet. If that’s what you’re looking for—this is the place to go! 🌟👏
